goal.en: Listen to feedback, ask for examples, and show how you'll improve.
goal.zh: 聽取回饋、請對方舉例，並說出你要怎麼改進。

background: small quiet meeting room for one-on-one talks, two armchairs facing each other, a low coffee table with two mugs, a floor lamp with a warm glow, a window with blinds half closed

intro.en: It's your monthly one-on-one with Ms. Wong. She has a notebook open and a friendly smile.
intro.zh: 今天是你和王經理每個月的一對一面談。她打開筆記本，面帶微笑。

intro.en: You're doing well, Kai. I just want to talk about your emails to clients. Some of them are a bit long.
intro.zh: 你表現得不錯，凱。我只是想聊聊你寫給客戶的信。有些寫得有點長。

lines.en: Clients are busy, so they sometimes miss the important part.
lines.zh: 客戶都很忙，所以有時候會漏看重要的部分。

choices.en: Thanks for the feedback. Could you give me an example?
choices.zh: 謝謝您的回饋。可以舉個例子嗎？
choices.tip: 先感謝，再請對方舉例，表示你願意聽，也想知道具體怎麼改。

choices.en: But long emails show I really care. Short ones look a bit lazy.
choices.zh: 但寫長一點代表我很用心。寫太短看起來有點偷懶。

lines.en: I'm not saying you don't care, Kai. I'm saying clients aren't reading them.
lines.zh: 我不是說你不用心，凱。我是說客戶沒在看。

story.en: The talk turns into a debate about email length. You win the debate, and the clients keep missing your questions.
story.zh: 面談變成一場信件長度辯論賽。你贏了辯論，客戶還是一直漏看你的問題。

fail.why: 一聽到回饋就急著辯解，對方會覺得你聽不進去。先說 Thanks for the feedback.，再問 Could you give me an example?。

choices.en: I'm so sorry. Maybe I'm just not good enough for this job.
choices.zh: 真的很抱歉。也許我就是不夠格做這份工作。

lines.en: Oh, no, no! Kai, it's just about emails. You're doing great.
lines.zh: 喔，不不不！凱，這只是信件的事。你做得很好。

story.en: Ms. Wong spends the whole meeting cheering you up. She never gets to tell you how to fix the emails.
story.zh: 王經理整場面談都在幫你打氣，根本沒機會告訴你信要怎麼改。

fail.why: 把一個小建議當成對自己的全盤否定，會讓對方不敢再給回饋。回饋是針對事情，不是針對你：Thanks for the feedback. Could you give me an example?。

lines.en: Sure. In your email to Lakeside Hotel, your question was in the fifth paragraph.
lines.zh: 好啊。你寫給湖畔飯店的那封信，你的問題放在第五段。

choices.en: I see. So I should put the main question at the top?
choices.zh: 了解。所以我應該把主要的問題放在最前面？
choices.tip: 用 So I should...? 把對方的建議換句話說，確認自己真的理解了。

choices.en: I know, I know. I will be careful next time, okay?
choices.zh: 我知道、我知道。下次我會小心，好嗎？

lines.en: If you knew, why was it in the fifth paragraph?
lines.zh: 如果你知道，那為什麼還放在第五段？

story.en: Ms. Wong hears "stop talking." She closes her notebook early, and you never find out what the second problem was.
story.zh: 王經理聽到的是「別再說了」。她提早闔上筆記本，你也沒機會知道第二個問題是什麼。

fail.why: 中文「我知道、我知道」表示有在聽，但英文 I know, I know 聽起來像不耐煩。說 I see. So I should...? 確認理解。

choices.en: Oh. So the main question should put at the top, is it?
choices.zh: 喔，所以主要問題應該放在最上面，是嗎？

lines.en: The question should put...? Sorry, who's putting what?
lines.zh: 問題應該放……？抱歉，誰要放什麼？

story.en: It takes three tries to figure out the sentence. Ms. Wong adds "grammar" to her notes, just below "long emails."
story.zh: 試了三次才搞懂這句話。王經理在筆記本上「信太長」的下面，又加了一行「文法」。

fail.why: 問題不會自己「放」，要用被動：should be put，或改成 I should put the main question at the top?；附加問句 is it 也不對，直接用問句語調就好。

lines.en: Exactly. Also, last week's email to Harbor Café had the wrong delivery date.
lines.zh: 沒錯。還有，上週寄給 Harbor Café 的信，交貨日期寫錯了。

choices.en: That's my mistake. I'll double-check dates before I hit send.
choices.zh: 那是我的錯。以後寄出前我會再確認一次日期。
choices.tip: That's my mistake. 簡短承認錯誤，再說具體的改進方法，比一直道歉更專業。

choices.en: Oh, that date was from Sam. He gave me the wrong one.
choices.zh: 喔，那個日期是山姆給我的。是他給錯的。

lines.en: Maybe. But your name was on the email, Kai.
lines.zh: 也許吧。但信上署名的是你，凱。

story.en: Ms. Wong checks with Sam. He gave you the right date. Now there are two awkward conversations instead of one.
story.zh: 王經理去問了山姆，他給你的日期是對的。現在尷尬的對話從一場變成兩場。

fail.why: 被指出錯誤時先推給同事，會讓人覺得你不負責。自己寄出的信就由自己承擔：That's my mistake. I'll double-check...。

choices.en: Oh, right. By the way, is the team dinner still on Friday?
choices.zh: 喔，對。對了，團隊聚餐還是星期五嗎？

lines.en: Yes, it is. But Kai, I'm talking about the delivery date.
lines.zh: 對，是星期五。不過凱，我在說的是交貨日期。

story.en: Ms. Wong writes "changed the subject" in her notebook. At least now you know the dinner is on Friday.
story.zh: 王經理在筆記本寫下「轉移話題」。至少你現在知道聚餐是星期五了。

fail.why: 被指出錯誤時換話題，看起來像在逃避。先承認：That's my mistake.，再說怎麼改進。

lines.en: Great. Do you have any questions for me?
lines.zh: 很好。你有什麼問題想問我嗎？

choices.en: Yes. Is there anything else I could do better in meetings?
choices.zh: 有。開會的時候，我還有什麼可以做得更好的地方嗎？
choices.tip: 主動請對方多給建議，表示你把回饋當成成長的機會。

choices.en: Yes. So what is my score this month? Did I pass or not?
choices.zh: 有。那我這個月幾分？有沒有及格？

lines.en: Score? It's not an exam, Kai. It's just a chat about how things are going.
lines.zh: 分數？這又不是考試，凱。只是聊聊最近的狀況。

story.en: Ms. Wong draws a smiley face in her notebook and shows you. You are not sure if that means you passed.
story.zh: 王經理在筆記本上畫了一個笑臉給你看。你不確定這樣算不算及格。

fail.why: 一對一面談是雙向的交流，不是打分數的考試。可以問 Is there anything else I could do better?，讓對方給你更多建議。

choices.en: What else I can do better? Please tell me more my weak points.
choices.zh: 我還有什麼可以做得更好？請多告訴我我的缺點。

lines.en: More weak points? Kai, I just gave you two. Let's not make a list.
lines.zh: 更多缺點？凱，我剛才已經說了兩個，我們不用列清單吧。

story.en: You leave the room with two notes and a strange feeling that you asked to be criticized.
story.zh: 你帶著兩條筆記離開，總覺得自己剛剛是在主動討罵。

fail.why: 疑問句要倒裝：What else can I do better?；tell me more my weak points 語序也不對，而且 weak points 聽起來很負面。說 Is there anything else I could do better?。

lines.en: Actually, yes. You have good ideas, but you're quiet in meetings. Speak up a bit more.
lines.zh: 其實有。你的點子很好，但開會時太安靜了。可以多發言一點。

choices.en: That's really helpful. I'll work on it, starting with Thursday's meeting.
choices.zh: 這真的很有幫助。我會努力改進，就從星期四的會議開始。
choices.tip: I'll work on it. 表示會努力改進，加上具體的開始時間，讓對方看到你的行動。

choices.en: Okay! From now on, I will shout out my ideas loudly in every meeting.
choices.zh: 好！從現在開始，每次開會我都會大聲喊出我的點子。

lines.en: Shout? No, no. Just speak up. You don't need to shout.
lines.zh: 喊？不不不，只要多發言就好，不用用喊的。

story.en: In Thursday's meeting, you say your first idea so loudly that Daniel spills his coffee.
story.zh: 星期四開會時，你第一個點子說得太大聲，丹尼爾嚇得把咖啡灑了出來。

fail.why: speak up 是「多發言、說出想法」，不是「大聲喊」。回答 I'll work on it. 再加上具體行動就好。

choices.en: That's because other people talk too much. It's hard to find a chance.
choices.zh: 那是因為其他人話太多了。我很難找到機會說。

lines.en: Hmm. Everyone has to find their own chance, Kai.
lines.zh: 嗯……每個人都要自己找機會的，凱。

story.en: The meeting ends on a flat note. Ms. Wong writes one last word in her notebook. It looks like "excuses."
story.zh: 面談在冷淡的氣氛中結束。王經理在筆記本上寫下最後一個字，看起來像是「藉口」。

fail.why: 把問題推給別人，等於拒絕了這次回饋。先說 That's really helpful.，再說 I'll work on it. 和你的具體做法。

lines.en: Perfect. I'm looking forward to hearing your ideas on Thursday.
lines.zh: 很好。我很期待星期四聽到你的想法。

story.en: You listened, asked for examples, and made a plan. Your next email to a client is four lines long, with the question in line one.
story.zh: 你認真聽、請對方舉例，還訂了改進計畫。你寄給客戶的下一封信只有四行，問題就寫在第一行。

notes.explain: 收到建議時的第一句話。先感謝，表示你願意聽，不會急著辯解。也可以說 I appreciate the feedback.。

example.en: Thanks for the feedback. I'll keep that in mind.
example.zh: 謝謝你的回饋，我會記住的。

notes.en: Could you give me an example?
notes.explain: 回饋太籠統時，請對方舉例，才知道具體要怎麼改。語氣是好奇、想學，不是要挑戰對方。

example.en: You said my slides are busy. Could you give me an example?
example.zh: 你說我的投影片太雜，可以舉個例子嗎？

notes.explain: 表示接受建議並會持續改進，比 I will be careful 更積極。後面加上具體的時間或做法會更有說服力。

example.en: Good point about my timing. I'll work on it.
example.zh: 時間掌控的部分說得很對，我會努力改進。

notes.zh: 我知道、我知道。（語氣陷阱）
notes.explain: 中文重複「我知道」是表示有在聽，但英文 I know, I know 聽起來像「好啦，別再說了」，很不耐煩。改說 I see. 或 That makes sense.。
在很多英語系職場，一對一面談是雙向的交流，不是考試。主管給建議是想幫你成長，不是在否定你，所以不必過度道歉，也可以反過來請主管多給建議。

example.en: Is there anything I could do differently next month?
example.zh: 下個月有什麼我可以換個方式做的嗎？
